sheet-81-1.description: The left part of sheet 81 shows the south end of Ocean City from 51st Street at the top to 55th Street at the bottom, between the edge of the sheet beyond West Avenue on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east. West Avenue, Asbury Avenue, Central Avenue and Wesley Avenue run down the page, which is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The rail line lettered W.J. & S. R.R. runs in West Avenue and a second set of tracks curves along the left margin. The blocks are cut into long narrow numbered lots, 15 feet wide alleys run through the middle of each block, and the streets are marked as 60, 65, 70 or 100 feet wide. Building is sparse: a handful of frame dwellings stand on the Asbury and Central Avenue blocks between 51st and 53rd Streets and on the lower blocks near 54th Street, and a hose house with a reel and 500 feet of hose stands near Central Avenue and 55th Street. Most lots are vacant. Six inch water pipes are drawn in the cross streets and fire hydrants are marked at several corners. The sections of the town are numbered 1A, 2A, 4A, 5A, 8A, 9A, 11A and 12A in large figures, and the word Section is lettered diagonally across the blocks. The drawing ends on the east at Wesley Avenue and the blue band of the ocean, beyond which a heavy line divides it from the right part, which starts at 55th Street again, further along the shore. Ocean City is lettered at the top with the note One hose cart, 500 ft 2 1/2 inch hose.
notes: Modern names: 55th Street is East 55th Street, and 52nd Street is also East 52nd Street, in OpenStreetMap. Wesley Avenue does not exist in OpenStreetMap this far south.
West Avenue carried the W.J. & S. R.R. in 1909 and was left out of the control; 10 junctions of Asbury and Central Avenue with 51st to 55th Street fix the part.
The part ends at the heavy line east of the ocean strip, which separates it from part 2.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line (same orientation, grid rotation about -33): part 1 left, 51st to 55th St, West Av to the ocean (Asbury, Central, Wesley Av); part 2 right, 55th to 59th St, U.S. Life Saving Station near 58th St. W.J.&S.R.R. along West Av. Control from Asbury and Central Av only (Wesley Av not in OpenStreetMap this far south; OSM names the old West Av line '59th Street' from 55th to 59th, excluded).

sheet-81-2.description: The right part of sheet 81 continues the south end of Ocean City from 55th Street at the top to 59th Street at the bottom, between West Avenue on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, with Asbury, Central and Wesley Avenues crossing it. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The railroad lettered W.J. & S. R.R. and the 55th St. R.R. Station stand at the left edge on West Avenue, with a pair of curving tracks leaving the sheet below. The blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots with alleys, and the streets are marked as 60, 65 or 70 feet wide, with 6 inch water pipes in the cross streets. Building is thin and scattered: frame dwellings along Asbury and Central Avenues, the Union Church on the block above 56th Street, a building coloured blue, and on the shore block between 58th and 59th Streets the U.S.L. Station of the Life Saving Service, a boat house with its living quarters. Boat houses stand on pilings between West and Asbury Avenues and another at the foot of the block above 59th Street and a plank walk is drawn along 59th Street. A strip of hatched approach to the beach is drawn at 58th Street at the right, next to the beach. The ocean fills a blue band along the right edge, and Ocean City and the neighbouring sheet numbers 81 and 82 are printed in the margins. Section numbers such as 13A, 14A, 22A, 23A, 24A, 25A and 26A are printed in large figures and the word Section is lettered across the lower blocks.
notes: Modern names: 55th Street is East 55th Street in OpenStreetMap. OpenStreetMap also names the former West Avenue line 59th Street between 55th and 59th Street; those junctions were excluded from the control.
West Avenue carried the W.J. & S. R.R. in 1909 and was left out of the control; 10 junctions of Asbury and Central Avenue with 55th to 59th Street fix the part.
U.S.L. Station is lettered on the shore block between 58th and 59th Streets.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line (same orientation, grid rotation about -33): part 1 left, 51st to 55th St, West Av to the ocean (Asbury, Central, Wesley Av); part 2 right, 55th to 59th St, U.S. Life Saving Station near 58th St. W.J.&S.R.R. along West Av. Control from Asbury and Central Av only (Wesley Av not in OpenStreetMap this far south; OSM names the old West Av line '59th Street' from 55th to 59th, excluded).

sheet-82-1.description: The left part of sheet 82 shows a stretch of Ocean City from 30th Street at the top to 34th Street at the bottom, with a strip of the 34th to 35th Street block below, between West Avenue on the left and the Atlantic Ocean on the right. West, Asbury, Central and Wesley Avenues run down the page, which is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, as the compass rose near the top shows. The blocks are cut into long numbered lots with 15 foot alleys, the streets are marked 60, 65 or 70 feet wide, and a 6 inch water pipe runs along some of them with fire hydrants at the corners. Building is thin. The most important structure is the Ocean Rest Institution, a large three-storey building with wings on the block between Central and Wesley Avenues just below 30th Street. A scatter of frame dwellings lies along Asbury and West Avenues between 30th and 33rd Streets, and a cluster near 34th Street includes Colony Cottage, with a post office, and a hose house with a hose cart and 500 feet of 2 1/2 inch hose beside Central Avenue. The rail line lettered W.J. & S. R.R. is drawn in West Avenue at the left. Most of the lots to the east are still vacant. Large figures mark sections 1A to 11A and 253 to 259, and the word Section is lettered across several blocks. The blue strip of the ocean and a heavy double line along the right edge divide this part from part 2, and a scale bar and the Princeton University Library stamp appear near the foot. Ocean City is lettered at the top of the sheet.
notes: The 30th Street row lies at the top edge of the sheet; its junctions were measured from the drawn edge.
West Avenue carried the W.J. & S. R.R. in 1909 and was left out of the control; Wesley Avenue does not exist in OpenStreetMap this far south.
The Ocean Rest Institution is lettered in full as Ocean Rest R.C. Institution on the sheet.

100 ft. Two parts side by side: part 1 left, 30th to 34th St with the Ocean Rest Institution (rotation about -40); part 2 right, 47th to 51st St, almost empty, The Berkeley at 48th St (rotation about -36); the blocks below 50th St on part 2 are drawn at a slightly different angle (51st / Asbury rejected, 15.7 m).

sheet-82-2.description: The right part of sheet 82 shows Ocean City from 47th Street at the top to 51st Street at the bottom, between West Avenue on the left and the edge of the part, which lies beyond Central Avenue and carries the lettering for the ocean, on the right. Asbury Avenue and Central Avenue are the main avenues drawn, and West Avenue with its railroad is at the left edge. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The blocks are divided into long narrow numbered lots with alleys, the streets are marked as 60, 65 or 70 feet wide, and a 6 inch water pipe is drawn in the cross streets with hydrants at the corners. The area is almost empty. A few frame dwellings stand on the blocks next to Asbury and Central Avenues, and The Berkeley, a larger building on Central Avenue at 48th Street, is the one named building. Below 50th Street the blocks are drawn at a slightly different angle, as the grid begins to turn with the shore, and the number of the neighbouring sheet 81 is printed at the foot. Section numbers 13A to 27A are shown in large figures, with the sheet number 82 and the notation N.J.C.M. Vol. 4 at the top right, and Ocean City is lettered across the top blocks near 47th Street. Vertical lettering along the right edge, partly legible, marks where the drawing ends. The heavy line down the left side divides this part from part 1.
notes: West Avenue carried the railroad in 1909 and was left out of the control; the control rests on Asbury and Central Avenue junctions with 47th to 51st Street.
Below 50th Street the blocks are drawn at a slightly different angle, and the 51st Street junction with Asbury Avenue came out 15.7 m off and was rejected.

100 ft. Two parts side by side: part 1 left, 30th to 34th St with the Ocean Rest Institution (rotation about -40); part 2 right, 47th to 51st St, almost empty, The Berkeley at 48th St (rotation about -36); the blocks below 50th St on part 2 are drawn at a slightly different angle (51st / Asbury rejected, 15.7 m).

sheet-83.description: Sheet 83 covers the bay side of Ocean City from 14th Street to 18th Street, west of Bay Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Bay Avenue runs down the right side of the sheet, with a strip of lots east of it, and the Beach Thoroughfare, the channel behind the island, fills the left side. Pleasure Avenue follows the shore diagonally from the top of the sheet and then runs straight down to 16th Street. Between 14th and 16th Streets the land between Pleasure and Bay Avenues is platted into rows of small numbered lots on two streets marked Not Named. South of 16th Street the sheet shows a lagoon development: two winding dredged channels, Carnival Bayou and Venetian Bayou, joined by a short channel crossed by a bridge at 17th Street, with Sunset Passage leading out to the thoroughfare and Princess Pathway lettered beside them. The bayous are lined on both banks with narrow wedge-shaped lots, and 16th, 17th and 18th Streets are laid out along their edges. The whole sheet is almost unbuilt: only a few frame dwellings and stores stand near 14th Street and at the shore by Pleasure Avenue. Street widths of 40 to 60 feet are noted. The lagoons were later filled and the area rebuilt on another plan.
notes: Modern names: West 14th to West 18th Street west of Bay Avenue and East 14th to East 18th Street east of it in OpenStreetMap.
The two streets marked Not Named between 14th and 16th Streets correspond roughly to today's Bayview Place and Sunset Place; not used for control.
Bay Avenue / 17th Street, at the bridge between the bayous, was not detected; OpenStreetMap has a second Bay Avenue / West 17th Street node about 80 m off the old line (a loop with South Bay Avenue).
100 ft. Bay front 14th to 18th St: Pleasure Av, Bay Av, the Carnival Bayou and Venetian Bayou lagoon lots, Beach Thoroughfare. Lagoons since altered; control from Bay Av and the numbered streets.

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84 covers the southern part of the resort at Ocean City from 14th Street at the top to 18th Street at the bottom, and from Haven Avenue on the west across West, Asbury and Central Avenues to Wesley Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a north arrow in the upper right, and is one of the coarser-scale sheets that show the outer blocks of the island. The blocks are laid out as a regular grid of long narrow numbered lots running across the avenues. Building is thin: the dwellings are concentrated on the Asbury Avenue and Central Avenue blocks between 14th and 17th Streets, mostly small frame houses coloured yellow, while most of the lots west of West Avenue and all the blocks nearest the shore are vacant. The railroad line of the W.J. & S. R.R. is lettered in West Avenue. A 6 inch water pipe is drawn along 15th Street in the streets. The sheet is divided into numbered sections by large figures in the blocks, for example 243 to 252 and 9A to 19A. The beach is drawn as a blue strip along the right edge with a pier built on pilings projecting into the ocean between 16th and 17th Streets, and a small building stands on the beach near it. The shoreline curves in towards the foot of the sheet. The lettering Ocean City and Atlantic Ocean appears in the upper right, with the compass rose, and the scale bar and the Princeton University Library stamp are at the bottom right.
notes: Modern names: 14th, 16th and 17th Street are East 14th, East 16th and East 17th Street in OpenStreetMap; 15th and 18th Street keep their names.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue carried railroads in 1909 (West Avenue is lettered with the W.J. & S. R.R.); they were left out of the control because their modern lines do not match the drawn ones.
The pier on the beach between 16th and 17th Streets is lettered as built on pilings.
100 ft. 14th to 18th St, Haven Av to Wesley Av and the ocean; pier at 16th-17th St; sparse building.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85 shows a strip of Ocean City from 12th Street at the top to 14th Street at the bottom, between Haven Avenue on the west and Central Avenue on the east, with West Avenue and Asbury Avenue crossing the middle and 13th Street dividing the sheet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, as the compass rose shows. The west side is the working edge of the resort: the railroad lettered A.C.R.R. (Reading) runs down Haven Avenue, and the W.J. & S. R.R. line is drawn in West Avenue, with a spur curving off into the C.H. Shoemaker Lumber Co. yard at the top, which has lumber piles and a garage and store house with a gasoline tank. Lower on Haven Avenue stands the Jos. G. Champion Lumber Co., lumber yard, with sheds, a wagon shed, a lime and cement store, lumber storage, an office and a store house. Between Asbury and Central Avenues the blocks are built up with frame dwellings, with Liberty Fire Co No. 3 in the upper block and St. Augustine R.C. Church, with a priest's house, a bell tower and the note badly damaged by fire, on the block between 13th and 14th Streets. The blocks west of the railroad and the lower blocks between Haven and West Avenues are mostly vacant lots with numbers only. Four inch and six inch water pipes are drawn in several streets, and the sections are numbered 235 to 240 in large figures. Neighbouring sheet numbers 84, 86, 87 and 97 are printed at the edges, and the scale bar is at the foot.
notes: Modern names: 12th and 14th Street are East 12th and East 14th Street in OpenStreetMap; 13th Street keeps its name.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue carried railroads in 1909 and were left out of the control, so only Asbury and Central Avenue junctions with 12th, 13th and 14th Street (six points) fix the sheet.
St. Augustine R.C. Church is noted as badly damaged by fire.

50 ft. 12th to 14th St, Haven Av to Central Av; Shoemaker and Champion lumber yards on the railroad along Haven Av, Liberty Fire Co No. 3, St. Augustine R.C. Church. Control from Asbury and Central Av only.

sheet-86.description: Sheet 86 is the beach-front strip of Ocean City from 12th Street at the top to 14th Street at the bottom, between Central Avenue on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, with Wesley Avenue running down the middle and 13th Street crossing it. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, and the compass rose is in the upper right. Only the western third is built up: the blocks between Central and Wesley Avenues carry a row of frame dwellings, and The Lafayette, a boarding house or hotel of three storeys with basement, stands on the Central Avenue frontage just south of 13th Street. A fire alarm or hydrant mark is lettered at Central Avenue. East of Wesley Avenue the lots are numbered but empty. A strip drawn with yellow hatching and dashed edges runs diagonally from the upper right to the foot of the sheet beside Wesley Avenue and is lettered Old Board Walk (to be removed); short approaches branch from it at 12th and 13th Streets and again near 14th Street at the bottom. A second, lettered approach joins it near the top, close to the lettering Ocean Av. The beach itself is left blank and the surf line is drawn as a blue band that runs down the right-hand edge, with the lettering Atlantic Ocean in the margin.
notes: Modern names: 12th and 14th Street are East 12th and East 14th Street in OpenStreetMap; 13th Street keeps its name.

Ocean Avenue is lettered at the top but not drawn as a street on this sheet; it was left out of the control, which rests on Central and Wesley Avenue junctions with 12th, 13th and 14th Street (six points).
The old boardwalk is lettered as to be removed.
50 ft. 12th to 14th St, Central and Wesley Av to the ocean; The Lafayette; old boardwalk 'to be removed'; beach blank.

sheet-87.description: Sheet 87 shows the western part of the 10th to 12th Street blocks of Ocean City, from Haven Avenue at the left edge across West Avenue and Asbury Avenue to Central Avenue at the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose at the top left. The left third of the sheet is an industrial strip along the railroad that curves through the blocks beside Haven Avenue. At the top are the Ocean City Water Co. works, with a covered aerating basin of 52,000 gallons, an iron stand pipe 131 feet high of 188,000 gallons capacity, two pumps and a compressor, and beside it the Ocean City Electric Light Co. power house and its office. Below these are the City Gas Light Co. with its gas holder, and in the lower left the C. H. Shoemaker Lumber Co. yard with lumber sheds, lumber piles, a lime store and open coal bins. West Avenue is lettered in the street running down the page with a wide right of way, and the long blocks east of it are filled with small frame dwellings and outbuildings on narrow numbered lots, with rows of dwellings in the 10th to 11th Street blocks and some larger boarding houses and hotels lettered in the Asbury and Central Avenue blocks, among them Hotel Willard, The Oxford, Kathlu, Lester Cottage and The Colonnage, as well as the American Steam Laundry in the lower middle. Street widths of 60 to 85 feet are noted, and 6 and 12 inch water pipes are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the corners. Many lots in the lower blocks are vacant.
notes: Modern names: 10th, 11th and 12th Street are East 10th, East 11th and East 12th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue (railroad lines in 1909) were left out of the control, see the atlas notes; only Asbury and Central Avenue were matched.
50 ft. 10th to 12th St, Haven Av to Central Av; water works, electric light plant, gas works, Shoemaker lumber yard. Control from Asbury and Central Av (one hand-picked point).

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88 shows the blocks of Ocean City between 10th Street at the top and 12th Street at the bottom, from Central Avenue at the left edge across Wesley Avenue to Ocean Avenue, with the open ground beyond Ocean Avenue running out to the boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean at the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose at the upper right. The built-up part is the two blocks west of Wesley Avenue: frame dwellings and boarding houses on narrow numbered lots, with the larger hotels and houses of the resort among them, The Imperial, The Raleigh, The Oceanic and New Hartford, and Holy Trinity Episcopal Church (lighted by electricity, heated by furnace, with a 50 foot belfry) on the Central Avenue frontage between 10th and 11th Streets. East of Wesley Avenue the lots are mostly vacant, with a few cottages near Ocean Avenue, one of them a brick cottage of one storey. Beyond Ocean Avenue only the blocks are laid out in outline; the boardwalk, drawn as a pair of dashed lines with diagonal yellow hatching for the pavilions and approaches, and the shore of the Atlantic Ocean cross the right edge of the sheet from the upper right to the lower right. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants at the corners, and street widths of 60 to 80 feet are noted. The scale bar is at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Modern names: 10th, 11th and 12th Street are East 10th, East 11th and East 12th Street in OpenStreetMap.
The East 12th Street arms were measured from edges 37 to 39 ft apart against 60 ft in the parcels (street drawn narrower than the modern right of way); residuals stayed under 1.3 m.
The 1909 boardwalk and shoreline at the right edge lie well inland of today's.
The names The Raleigh, The Oceanic and New Hartford were read at reduced resolution and are medium confidence.
50 ft. 10th to 12th St, Central, Wesley and Ocean Av to the boardwalk and shore; hotels, Holy Trinity Church.

sheet-89.description: Sheet 89 covers two long blocks in the centre of Ocean City between 8th Street at the top and 10th Street at the bottom, from Asbury Avenue on the west to Ocean Avenue on the east, with 9th Street crossing the middle and Central and Wesley Avenues running between. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The Asbury Avenue frontage between 8th and 9th Streets is the commercial edge of the sheet: brick and frame stores, offices, halls on the second floor, a furniture store, bake houses, a green house, and the fire department station with a steam engine and combination wagon. Elsewhere the blocks are filled with frame dwellings and the boarding houses and small hotels of the resort: The Elberon, The Lorraine, The Strand, Hotel Mayberry, The Biscayne and the large Normandie-on-the-Sea on Ocean Avenue in the upper half, and The Atglen, The Fairview, The Waverly, Illinois on the Strand, The Traymore and The Swarthmore in the lower half. Ocean City High School, a brick building with heating by furnace and electric light, stands on the Central Avenue block between 8th and 9th Streets. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants at the corners and a fire alarm box at Asbury Avenue and 10th Street. Moorlyn Terrace is lettered at the right margin, leading off the sheet towards the beach (sheet 90). Many lots on the Ocean Avenue and lower Asbury Avenue blocks are still vacant. Street widths of 60 to 80 feet are noted at the corners.
notes: Modern names: 8th, 9th and 10th Street are East 8th, East 9th and East 10th Street in OpenStreetMap (east of Bay Avenue).

9th Street was left out of the control: all three of its junctions came out 6 m off in a fit to the 8th and 10th Street rows (modern 9th to 10th Street is 15 m longer than 8th to 9th, drawn equal); the modern street, the main causeway approach, has probably been widened or shifted.
50 ft. 8th to 10th St, Asbury Av to Ocean Av; Ocean City High School, Hotel Normandie-on-the-Sea. 9th St left out of control (modern line about 6 m off).

sheet-90.description: Sheet 90 covers the beach front of Ocean City between 8th Street at the top and 10th Street at the bottom, from Ocean Avenue on the left edge to the Atlantic Ocean, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Atlantic Avenue runs down the left third of the sheet between 8th and 9th Streets, with Moorlyn Terrace crossing it towards the boardwalk; south of 9th Street Atlantic Avenue is not opened and the whole tract to 10th Street is a single large lot with a few small frame dwellings. The boardwalk runs diagonally down the right side of the sheet along the beach, with approaches from the streets, and the amusement and bathing buildings of the resort stand along it, many iron clad and built on piles: a bowling alley and dance hall and the Public Pavilion on a pier near 8th Street, the Hippodrome and a moving picture show near Moorlyn Terrace, and between 9th and 10th Streets the carrousel and stands of Fogg's enterprises, Fogg's Pier Theatre on a pier, Shriver's baths and bath houses, and Boyle's Baths. Inland the blocks along Ocean and Atlantic Avenues are almost empty, with a few frame dwellings at Moorlyn Terrace. Water pipes are drawn in 8th and 9th Streets. Street widths of 60 and 70 feet are noted. The shore line and boardwalk shown here have since been moved seaward, and the sheet is placed from the junctions of Ocean Avenue, Atlantic Avenue, 8th Street, Moorlyn Terrace and 10th Street only.
notes: Modern names: East 8th, East 9th and East 10th Street in OpenStreetMap.
9th Street was left out of the control (displaced about 6 m in the modern data, see sheet 89); Atlantic Avenue is not drawn south of 9th Street, so its junction with 10th Street was excluded.
Ocean Avenue / 8th Street and Ocean Avenue / 10th Street are hand-picked: Ocean Avenue lies on the left edge of the sheet with only its east side drawn.
50 ft. 8th to 10th St, Ocean Av and Atlantic Av to the boardwalk; Moorlyn Terrace; Hippodrome, Public Pavilion, Fogg's Pier Theatre, bath houses. Few junctions.

sheet-91.description: Sheet 91 covers the resort blocks of Ocean City between 6th Street at the top and 8th Street at the bottom, from Central Avenue at the left across Wesley, Ocean and Atlantic Avenues to the right edge, with 7th Street running through the middle and Plymouth Place cutting the lower right blocks. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose in the upper right. The sheet is the heart of the boarding house district. The blocks along Central and Wesley Avenues hold frame dwellings and boarding houses, among them the Park Hotel at the top left, the First M.E. Church with its electric light and furnace heat at the lower left, and the Presbyterian church between Wesley and Ocean Avenues, drawn in blue with its lot. Larger hotels and apartment houses stand near the beach end: Hotel Brighton on the block next to Ocean Avenue, White Hall (boarding), The Scarborough, apartments, Gale Apartments near Atlantic Avenue, and a row along the foot of the sheet on 8th Street lettered St. George, St. Charles, The Sterling and The Headam, each of four storeys with open first and second floors. Smaller cottages fill Plymouth Place. A few lots between Wesley and Ocean Avenues remain vacant. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at corners, and street widths of 60 to 70 feet are noted. A scale bar is at the foot. Atlantic Avenue at the right edge is the beach front street, with the boardwalk shown on sheet 92.
notes: Modern names: 6th, 7th and 8th Street are East 6th, East 7th and East 8th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Plymouth Place was not used as control.
The word PARK is lettered along the top margin (probably Park Place), not entered as a street name.
50 ft. 6th to 8th St, Central Av to Atlantic Av; Plymouth Pl; Park Hotel, Hotel Brighton, Presbyterian and First M.E. churches.

sheet-92.description: Sheet 92 covers the beach front between 6th Street and 8th Street, east of Atlantic Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Atlantic Avenue runs along the left edge of the sheet, and 6th Street, 7th Street, Plymouth Place and 8th Street cross from it to the boardwalk, which runs diagonally along the right side of the sheet with approaches at the street ends; the Atlantic Ocean lies beyond. The land between 6th and 7th Streets is one large undivided tract, with a row of four small frame dwellings near 6th Street. Between 7th Street and Plymouth Place are only two or three frame buildings, and a row of three dwellings faces Plymouth Place from the south. The bathing establishments of the beach front occupy the block between Plymouth Place and 8th Street: the Bellevue Baths of S. Church & Son, a long row of bath houses with platforms, and Doughty's Baths, bath houses built on piles, with other bath houses and stands along the boardwalk and a small pier near 8th Street. Park land is lettered beyond 6th Street at the top. Street widths of 50 to 70 feet are noted. The shore and boardwalk have since been moved seaward.
notes: Modern names: East 6th, East 7th and East 8th Street in OpenStreetMap.
All four control points lie along Atlantic Avenue, so the sheet is written with a helmert transformation (position, scale and rotation only); low confidence away from Atlantic Avenue.
50 ft. 6th to 8th St east of Atlantic Av to the boardwalk; Plymouth Pl; Bellevue Baths, Doughty's Baths. Junctions only along Atlantic Av. Placed by helmert from the four Atlantic Av junctions.

sheet-93.description: Sheet 93 shows the railroad district of Ocean City between 8th Street at the top and 10th Street at the bottom, from Simpson Avenue at the left across Haven Avenue and West Avenue to Asbury Avenue at the right, with 9th Street crossing the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose near the centre. Two railroad lines, the Atlantic City R.R. (Reading) and the W.J. & S. R.R., converge from the west and run through the sheet in several tracks and sidings, one curving in from the upper left and another running down the page beside West Avenue. The left half and centre are mostly vacant numbered lots on the Simpson and Haven Avenue blocks, with the Macedonia M.E. Church (lighted by electricity, heated by furnace) in the lower left, an Ocean City Depot with a freight house on the Haven Avenue side near 10th Street, and the Herdley and Adams wood working mill and lumber sheds, powered from the electric light plant, at the foot. A second Ocean City Depot with its freight house stands beside West Avenue near the top. The built-up part is the strip west of Asbury Avenue, with stores and shops along the Asbury frontage: the 1st Baptist Church, The Ledger electric power printing office, the Ocean City Garage (iron clad), a plumber and a drug store, and dwellings behind them. Water pipes of 4, 8 and 12 inches are drawn in the streets. Many of the blocks are laid out on narrow lots with no buildings.
notes: Modern names: 8th, 9th and 10th Street are East 8th, East 9th and East 10th Street in OpenStreetMap.

Only 3 junctions were used (Asbury Avenue with 8th and 10th Street, Simpson Avenue with 10th Street): Haven Avenue and West Avenue carried railroads, 9th Street is displaced in the modern data, and the modern 8th Street to Simpson Avenue junction is about 110 ft off the drawn spacing.
Building names were read at full resolution; the railroad lettering was not checked at full resolution.

50 ft. 8th to 10th St, Simpson Av to Asbury Av; Atlantic City R.R. (Reading) and W.J.&S.R.R. tracks and the Ocean City depots; Macedonia M.E. Church, Herdley & Adams wood working. Only 3 junctions usable (Haven, West Av railroads, 9th St displaced, Simpson / 8th off the drawn spacing): low confidence.

sheet-94.description: Sheet 94 covers the commercial centre of Ocean City between 6th Street at the top and 8th Street at the bottom, from Haven Avenue near the left edge across West Avenue and Asbury Avenue to Central Avenue at the right, with 7th Street crossing the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose at the top left. The two eastern blocks, along Asbury and Central Avenues, are the downtown: rows of brick and frame stores, with halls on the 2nd and 3rd floors, drug stores, an ice cream parlour, offices, a post office in the Bourse Building at the foot of Asbury Avenue and 8th Street, and The Sentinel printing office run on electric power. The centre of the sheet is taken by the Ocean City Ice and Coal Co. works, with an ice house, coal bin, freezing tanks, ice machinery and engine room, a cream factory, wood cutting shop and condensers. The railroad lines, marked P. & R. R. and W. J. & S. R. R. in the margins, run diagonally across the left and lower left and along West Avenue. On the Haven Avenue blocks to the west stand the St. James A.M.E. Church (heated by stoves, lighted by electricity), the Tabernacle Baptist Church at the lower left, wagon sheds, a large warehouse or wood working shop marked as being built, and many vacant lots. Water pipes are drawn in the streets and street widths of 60 to 80 feet noted.
notes: Modern names: 6th, 7th and 8th Street are East 6th, East 7th and East 8th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue (railroads in 1909) were left out of the control; only Asbury and Central Avenue junctions were used.
The word PARK is lettered along the top margin and was not entered as a street name.
50 ft. 6th to 8th St, Haven Av to Central Av; downtown Asbury Av blocks, fire department, Ocean City Ice and Coal Co., Tabernacle Baptist Church. Control from Asbury and Central Av.

sheet-95.description: Sheet 95 shows the north end of Ocean City between 1st Street at the top and 5th Street at the foot, from the shore of Great Egg Harbor Bay at the left across Bay, Simpson, Haven, West and Asbury Avenues to Central Avenue at the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose at the upper left. Most of the sheet is a regular grid of narrow numbered lots, many of them vacant, with scattered dwellings and outbuildings that thicken towards the lower right, in the blocks along Asbury and Central Avenues. A railroad line (Atlantic City R.R.) runs down the page beside Haven Avenue and curves off to the west across the blocks at 2nd Street, with a second line beside West Avenue; the F. J. Smith lumber yard, with its sheds, lime and carpenter shops, stands beside the line at 4th Street, with a turn table to the south. Along the bay shore at the left, the water is shown in blue and the shore is lined with boat houses, a Longport Boat Landing and several piers and walks built on piles that run out into the bay. Street widths are noted on the avenues and the blocks are numbered. A scale bar of 100 feet to one inch is at the foot, and the word Park is lettered along the bottom margin.
notes: Modern names: 4th Street is East 4th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue (railroads in 1909) were left out of the control.
The bay shore, piers and boat houses at the left edge differ from the present shoreline.
100 ft. 1st to 5th St, Great Egg Harbor Bay front to Central Av (Bay, Simpson, Haven, West, Asbury Av); boat landings and railroad.

sheet-96.description: Sheet 96 covers the southern end of the first group of numbered blocks of Ocean City, between 1st Street at the top and 5th Street at the foot, from Central Avenue at the left edge across Wesley and Ocean Avenues to Atlantic Avenue, and beyond Atlantic Avenue to the beach. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, marked by a compass rose at the right. West of Atlantic Avenue the blocks are laid out in long numbered lots, mostly vacant, with dwellings and a few larger houses such as The Arlington gathered at the lower left near Central Avenue and 4th and 5th Streets, and some small buildings lettered as iron clad. East of Atlantic Avenue the ground is cut by short east to west places lettered Saint Charles, Delancey, Park and Brighton Place, with narrow lots numbered on each side; the places carry only a scattering of new frame dwellings, and the lots stretch out to the beach at the right edge, where the approaches to the boardwalk are drawn in dashed outline with yellow hatching. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the avenues, and street widths of 70 feet are noted. A scale bar of 100 feet to one inch is at the foot, with the word Park lettered along the bottom margin.
notes: Modern names: 4th Street is East 4th Street in OpenStreetMap.
The places east of Atlantic Avenue were not used as control.
The place names are lettered ST. CHARLES PL., DELANCEY PL., PARK PL. and BRIGHTON PL. (read here on the first and last at full resolution; Delancey and Park from the overview).
100 ft. 1st to 5th St, Central Av to the beach (Wesley, Ocean, Atlantic Av) and St Charles, Delancey, Park and Brighton Pl.

sheet-97-1.description: The main part of sheet 97 shows the bay front of Ocean City from 10th Street to 14th Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Great Egg Harbor Bay fills the left side of the part, and its shore runs irregularly down the sheet with docks, plank walks and small piers. Bay Avenue, Simpson Avenue and Haven Avenue cross the part from top to bottom; 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th and 14th Streets cross it from the bay. Between 10th and 12th Streets the land west of Bay Avenue is still undivided and the shore is lined with boat builders and boat houses: H. F. Sailor boat builder on piles, Simmons, Jos. G. Champion, A. D. Scull, Fogg, Smith, Carson, Mrs. Sam Dixon, F. G. Riggins, Schermerhorn, Geo. Barett and the Quaker Boat House, with marsh land noted beyond the top of the sheet. Between 12th and 13th Streets the Bay View Pavilion and a row of dwellings with boat houses and auto houses face the water. South of 13th Street the shore turns south-west, Pleasure Avenue runs along it diagonally, and Marine Place crosses from Pleasure Avenue to Bay Avenue, with small lots numbered on both sides. East of Bay Avenue the blocks are platted into narrow lots with few buildings, mostly frame dwellings, and a row of identical double dwellings faces Bay Avenue between 12th and 13th Streets. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. The strip to the left of the heavy dividing line belongs to the other parts of this sheet.
notes: Modern names: the numbered streets are East 10th to East 14th Street east of Bay Avenue and West 12th to West 14th Street west of it in OpenStreetMap.
The bay shore has since been filled and built over west of Bay Avenue between 10th and 12th Streets.
Haven Avenue was left out of the control: it carried the Atlantic City (Reading) railroad in 1909 and its junctions were 2 to 8 m off; without it the fit RMSE fell from 1.14 to 0.56 m.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 right, bay front 10th to 14th St (Bay Av, Simpson Av, Haven Av, Pleasure Av, Marine Pl) with boat builders; part 2 upper left, bay front at 6th and 7th St (Pleasure Av, Bay Av), Ocean City Yacht Club; part 3 lower left below a heavy line, 19th to 21st St, West Av to Central Av.

sheet-97-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 97 is an inset of the bay front at 6th and 7th Streets, drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same orientation as the rest of the sheet, with north towards the upper left. It is separated from the rest of the sheet by heavy lines on its right and lower sides; Bay Avenue runs along the right-hand line. Great Egg Harbor Bay occupies the left half of the inset, and its shore is lined with boat houses, piers and inclines. Pleasure Avenue runs parallel to the shore between it and Bay Avenue, and 6th Street and 7th Street cross from the bay to Bay Avenue. On the shore between 6th and 7th Streets stand the Ocean City Yacht Club, H. C. Smith's boat house and boat shop, and L. Risley, boat builder, with several smaller boat houses on piers; there is another boat house south of 7th Street. Between Pleasure Avenue and Bay Avenue the block is still almost empty, with one frame dwelling. North of 6th Street the land between the shore and Bay Avenue is undivided. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in Pleasure Avenue and 7th Street, with a hydrant on Pleasure Avenue. Street widths of 60 and 75 feet are noted.
notes: Modern names: West 6th Street and West 7th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from four junctions only (fit RMSE 0.16 m, no leave-one-out); the bay shore has since been moved out by filling.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 right, bay front 10th to 14th St (Bay Av, Simpson Av, Haven Av, Pleasure Av, Marine Pl) with boat builders; part 2 upper left, bay front at 6th and 7th St (Pleasure Av, Bay Av), Ocean City Yacht Club; part 3 lower left below a heavy line, 19th to 21st St, West Av to Central Av.

sheet-97-3.description: The lower left part of sheet 97 is an inset showing the blocks between 19th Street and 20th Street, with parts of the blocks above and below, from West Avenue to just east of Central Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same orientation as the rest of the sheet, with north towards the upper left, and is cut off from the bay-front part by a heavy line along its top and right sides. Asbury Avenue and Central Avenue run down the inset between West Avenue on the left and the dividing line on the right; the tracks of the W.J. & S. R.R. are lettered in West Avenue. The blocks are platted into narrow numbered lots, almost all vacant: only a few frame dwellings stand on the Asbury Avenue and Central Avenue frontages between 19th and 20th Streets. Water pipes and a hydrant are drawn in Central Avenue, and street widths of 60 and 70 feet are noted. The inset lies well to the south-west of the rest of the sheet on the ground, between sheets 84 and the undrawn blocks beyond.
notes: West Avenue was left out of the control: it carries the W.J. & S. R.R. tracks on the sheet, and its two junctions disagreed by about 90 px (7 m).
Placed from four junctions (Asbury and Central Avenue at 19th and 20th Street; fit RMSE 0.17 m, no leave-one-out).

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 right, bay front 10th to 14th St (Bay Av, Simpson Av, Haven Av, Pleasure Av, Marine Pl) with boat builders; part 2 upper left, bay front at 6th and 7th St (Pleasure Av, Bay Av), Ocean City Yacht Club; part 3 lower left below a heavy line, 19th to 21st St, West Av to Central Av.

sheet-98-1.description: The upper part of sheet 98 shows the north end of Ocean City between 1st Street, along the heavy line at the bottom of the part, and the blocks beyond North Street, from Great Egg Harbor Bay to Central Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. South of North Street the avenues keep their town names, Bay, Simpson, Haven, West, Asbury and Central Avenues; north of it they continue as Bay Road, Simpson Road, Station Road West, Station Road East, Asbury Road and Central Road. The tracks of the Philadelphia & Reading railroad are lettered in Haven Avenue and those of the W.J. & S. R.R. in West Avenue, and both lines end at North Street; between Station Road West and Station Road East a large block north of North Street is left undivided. A tidal creek marked with the mean tide line winds along the east side of Bay Avenue and Bay Road, and a row of lots west of Bay Road faces the bay. The whole part is platted into narrow numbered lots. Only the blocks between West Avenue and Central Avenue near 1st Street are built on, with a few dozen frame dwellings; the rest is vacant. The lettering Ocean City Gardens and North Point Section is spread across the area. Water pipes are drawn in 1st Street, and street widths of 60 to 100 feet are noted.
notes: Modern names: North is North Street; Station Road West and Station Road East are West Station Road and East Station Road in OpenStreetMap; East Station Road now meets North Street at West Avenue.
Haven Avenue and West Avenue were left out of the control: both carried railroad tracks on the sheet and their junctions were 3 to 5 m off; without them the fit RMSE fell from 3.0 to 0.23 m.

100 ft. Two parts, same orientation, separated by a heavy line: part 1 upper, North Point north of 1st St from Bay Road to Central Road (Simpson Road, Station Road West and East, Asbury Road, North St); part 2 lower, Ocean City Gardens north of 1st St from Central Av to Atlantic Av (Battersea Road, Laurel Road, Atlantic Blvd, Morningside Road, St James Pl).

sheet-98-2.description: The lower part of sheet 98 is the ocean side of the north end of Ocean City, from Central Avenue east to the beach and from 1st Street north into Ocean City Gardens. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, at the same orientation as the upper part (north towards the upper left), but placed below it on the page; on the ground it lies to the east of the upper part. The lower blocks, between 1st Street and North Street, are laid out on the town grid along Central, Wesley, Ocean and Atlantic Avenues, with Saint James Place running east from Atlantic Avenue towards the beach. North of North Street the Ocean City Gardens plan begins: Central Road and Wesley Road continue the avenues, Laurel Road and Battersea Road cut diagonally across, Ocean Road curves north-east, and the broad Atlantic Boulevard and Morningside Road sweep round in wide arcs, with Pinnacle Road at the top. Every block is divided into narrow numbered lots, and the part is almost entirely vacant: one or two frame dwellings stand on Central Avenue and one on Ocean Avenue. The area beyond Morningside Road is left blank. An approach to the boardwalk is noted at the lower right corner, and a water pipe is drawn in 1st Street. Street widths of 60 to 100 feet are noted.
notes: Modern names: North is North Street in OpenStreetMap.

The 1st Street junctions at Ocean and Atlantic Avenues and Atlantic Avenue / Saint James Place were rejected by the fit (9 to 18 m): the detector paired lot lines there; the part is placed from the other 12 junctions, including the Gardens roads.

100 ft. Two parts, same orientation, separated by a heavy line: part 1 upper, North Point north of 1st St from Bay Road to Central Road (Simpson Road, Station Road West and East, Asbury Road, North St); part 2 lower, Ocean City Gardens north of 1st St from Central Av to Atlantic Av (Battersea Road, Laurel Road, Atlantic Blvd, Morningside Road, St James Pl).
